> OrangeOS: a cyberdeck with its own distro I'm building a cyberdeck around a Raspberry Pi 5 (16 GB kit), and since I got the priciest part for a good price, I figured: why not make my own distro for it too? I'll document the whole journey with a wiring diagram, a parts list, and config tweaks (like speeding up a slow Pi fan) you can use before flashing. I'll also write a step-by-step tutorial and keep the build cheap so anyone can make their own. Yes, I'll use AI, but to help me learn Linux and coding, not to do the work for me. OrangeOS will be as modular as possible. For example, I plan to add an ESP32 with a small screen showing temps and battery life. People will say to use an Orange Pi to match the branding, but I'm sticking with the Pi 5 since I already have it. Expect a few sleepless nights!
